stories.title: Prateek built business empire away from politics:17 companies linked to family associates; daughters inherit crores worth of assets and properties
stories.summary: Real estate ventures, a lavish bungalow, premium gyms, a ₹5-crore Lamborghini, and a royal lifestyle — these defined the public image of Prateek Yadav, the younger son of late Samajwadi Party founder Mulayam Singh Yadav. Prateek, who stayed away from active politics and built his identity in the real estate and fitness industries, died at the age of 38. The cause of death has been reported as cardiac arrest. His wife, Aparna Yadav, is a BJP leader and currently serves as Vice-Chairperson of the Uttar Pradesh State Women Commission. Let's find out how much wealth and what legacy Prateek, who built his own world amidst political influence, has left behind... Successful businessman, but no company registered in his name Unlike other members of the Yadav political family, Prateek Yadav was not directly associated with politics. He completed his education at the University of Leeds and was regarded as a successful businessman. However, official records reportedly show that no company was directly registered in his name. According to government documents, Prateek owned movable and immovable assets worth nearly ₹19.56 crore, including ₹13.41 crore in movable assets and ₹6.15 crore in immovable property. Among these assets was a Lamborghini worth ₹5.21 crore. Reports say he had taken a loan of ₹4.5 crore from Union Bank of India to purchase the luxury car. His annual income from business and assets was said to be ₹1.47 crore, according to details mentioned in Aparna Yadav’s election affidavit during the 2015-16 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Indirect links to multiple companies Sources close to the family and company documents suggest that Prateek was never officially listed as a director or designated director in any company. However, he allegedly maintained indirect control over several firms. Most of these businesses were reportedly operated in the names of Aparna Yadav’s brother Aman Singh Bisht and close associates. Aman Bisht linked to 17 companies After the Samajwadi Party formed the government in Uttar Pradesh in 2012, Aman Bisht and his associates reportedly established 17 companies by May 2018. These companies included Fame Infra City, Fame Sky Ventures, Sunshine Sky Ventures, Guiding Tree, ACME Skyventures, Shri Shekhar Infratech Private Limited, Shri Shakti Infrazone Private Limited, Monal Infraheights Private Limited, Shukra Construction Private Limited, DB Infrazone Private Limited, Robust Real Buildcon Private Limited, Robust Realtors Private Limited, and Robust Residency Private Limited. People familiar with the matter claimed that the operational control of these companies remained with Prateek Yadav. Reports of disputes between Aman Bisht and Prateek over financial transactions involving these firms had also surfaced in the past. Owned luxury property in Lucknow Prateek built a lavish residence in Gautampalli, a high-security and upscale locality in Lucknow’s Hazratganj area. He lived there with Aparna Yadav and their two daughters, Prathama and Padmaja. The house is located on Vikramaditya Marg, considered one of Lucknow’s most elite residential zones. Apart from this, Prateek reportedly owned 22 bighas of agricultural land in Ramaiyapur village near Lucknow. He also possessed a 5,123-square-foot residential building on Mahatma Gandhi Marg in the Cantonment area. Built ‘Iron Core Fit’ into a fitness brand Prateek Yadav was highly active in the fitness industry. In 2015, he launched a fitness brand called Iron Core Fit, which later expanded into multiple branches. Sources said the gym featured imported fitness equipment from abroad. Annual membership fees reportedly went up to ₹35,000. He also operated another major gym near Manoj Pandey Chauraha in Gomti Nagar, Lucknow. Apart from gyms, he was involved in fitness training, brand promotions, and wellness consulting. Prateek was also active on social media, where he frequently shared workout videos and fitness tips. Many followers viewed him as a fitness icon. No property in Saifai despite Yadav family roots Although the political identity of the Yadav family is closely tied to Saifai, Prateek reportedly owned neither land nor a house there. Family sources said that whenever he visited Saifai, he stayed at Mulayam Singh Yadav’s residence. However, Prateek and his family rarely stayed there and mostly visited only during family events or major Samajwadi Party functions. Personal life and relationship with Aparna Yadav Prateek’s mother, Sadhana Gupta, married Chandra Prakash Gupta in 1986, and Prateek was born in 1987. The couple divorced in 1990, after which Sadhana grew close to Mulayam Singh Yadav. Mulayam married Sadhana Gupta in 2003 and publicly accepted Prateek as his son. Prateek married Aparna Yadav in a love marriage around 14 years ago. Earlier this year, on January 19, he unexpectedly announced his decision to divorce Aparna, accusing her of making his life “hell.” However, the couple reconciled within nine days. Prateek later shared a photograph with Aparna on Instagram and captioned it, “All is Good.” Death and Funeral Prateek Yadav died at around 6 am on May 13 at the age of 38. His post-mortem report cited cardiac arrest as the cause of death, though viscera samples have been preserved for further examination. His last rites were performed on May 14 in Lucknow. Aparna Yadav’s father, Arvind Singh Bisht, lit the funeral pyre. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav paid his final respects by placing wood on his brother’s pyre.

stories.title: Medical costs rising sharply in UP:Even 5-year-olds facing stress; over 70% people depend on private hospitals
stories.summary: Two incidents from Uttar Pradesh highlight how rising medical expenses are pushing families into severe financial distress: These cases underline the growing healthcare burden in the state. A recent National Statistics Office (NSO) survey revealed that people in Uttar Pradesh spent nearly ₹28,000 crore from their own pockets on medical treatment between January and December 2025. Treatment cost higher in rural government hospitals A National Statistics Office (NSO) survey titled Household Social Consumption: Health revealed that patients in Uttar Pradesh spend an average of ₹14,000 even when admitted to government hospitals. Surprisingly, treatment costs in rural government hospitals are higher than in urban ones. According to the survey, treatment in an urban government hospital costs an average of ₹10,547, while patients in rural government hospitals spend around ₹16,650. Expenses rise sharply in private hospitals, about ₹75,000 in urban private hospitals and nearly ₹38,000 in rural private hospitals. Private hospitals cost 6–7 times more for common illnesses The survey found that treatment for seasonal illnesses such as cold, cough, and fever is 6–7 times more expensive in private hospitals compared to government facilities. Treatment for such illnesses costs around ₹466 in a rural government hospital, while the same treatment in a private hospital costs nearly ₹2,457. Normal delivery costs over ₹31,000 in private hospitals The survey also highlighted the sharp difference in maternity expenses. The average cost of a normal delivery in a government hospital is ₹2,607, while the same procedure in a private hospital costs around ₹31,137. Overall, the average delivery expense stands at ₹13,434. Trust in private doctors instead of government doctors In UP, 8 out of every 100 are sick NSO conducted a survey in 1192 rural and 700 urban blocks of UP between January and December 2025. In this, health-related information of 80,477 people from 15,096 families was collected. In the survey, the pattern of people falling ill was observed over two types of time periods. The survey revealed that 8 out of 100 people in UP fall ill every 15 days. This figure is lower than the national average of 13. The highest number is in Kerala, where 25 out of 100 people fall ill every 15 days. Children troubled by infection, youth by digestion, and elderly by heart problems According to the NSO survey, last year, 26% of patients admitted to hospitals were under 30 years of age. Meanwhile, 45% of children up to 14 years of age had to be admitted to the hospital due to infection. Digestion-related problems were more common among patients aged 15 to 44 years. About 15% of those admitted were due to this. Heart diseases were found to be more prevalent among patients above 45 years of age. The UP government spent about 17 thousand crore rupees in 2025-26 on facilities like free medicines, free tests, ambulances, and vaccinations (which directly benefit the common man). However, the government's health budget was 50 thousand crore rupees. This also includes expenses like salaries, pensions, and infrastructure.

stories.title: Storms lash 37 UP districts with strong winds:Putin condoles loss of 111 lives in storm across state
stories.summary: Severe storms, heavy rain, and strong winds have claimed 111 lives across Uttar Pradesh over the last two days, while large parts of the state now brace for an intense heatwave. The worst-hit districts were Prayagraj, where 21 people died, and Bhadohi, which reported 17 deaths. Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed condolences over the tragedy. In a message to Indian President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Putin said he was deeply saddened by the heavy loss of life and widespread destruction caused by the storms in Uttar Pradesh. CM Yogi orders relief measures Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath directed ministers in charge of districts to visit affected families and assess the situation on the ground. “In this hour of disaster, the government stands firmly with the people. Any negligence in relief operations will not be tolerated,” the Chief Minister said. Trees uprooted, tin roofs blown away On Thursday, strong winds accompanied by rain hit the Rajghat area, about 25 km from Lalitpur headquarters. Several trees were uprooted, while a tin roof was blown off a house. On Wednesday evening, storms lashed nearly 30 districts, including Ghaziabad, Varanasi, and Ayodhya. Rain and hailstorms damaged property in several places. Trees collapsed, electricity poles were uprooted, and vehicles were damaged after walls fell. In Bareilly, a 50-year-old man was reportedly lifted nearly 50 feet into the air along with a tin shed during winds blowing at 90 kmph. He fell into a field nearly 100 metres away and suffered a fractured arm. After treatment at a hospital, he was discharged. Wednesday's weather pictures Heatwave warning for Bundelkhand and Southern UP According to the Meteorological Department, heatwave conditions are expected on Friday in Banda, Hamirpur, Mahoba, Jhansi, Lalitpur, Prayagraj, Fatehpur, Chitrakoot, and Kaushambi. This hands-on experience revealed operational realities often missed by senior management, highlighting how distance from the ground floor can compromise decision-making. Leaders must actively seek firsthand understanding to avoid blind spots and improve workflows.

stories.title: Imam, 54, who claimed ‘jinn powers’ jailed for life over abuse crimes against women and girls
stories.summary: A former East London imam, Abdul Halim Khan, has been jailed for life after being convicted of 21 sexual offences, including rape and child rape, against seven victims over a decade. He exploited his religious authority, claiming supernatural powers to manipulate and abuse vulnerable women and children. The case highlights safeguarding failures and barriers victims face when reporting abuse.

stories.title: Buckingham Palace hosts historic meeting between King Charles and New Zealand’s Māori Queen
stories.summary: New Zealand's Māori Queen, Ngā Wai Hono i te Pō, met King Charles III at Buckingham Palace, marking a significant moment for Commonwealth ties. The meeting highlighted discussions on climate challenges, Indigenous leadership, and youth empowerment, aligning with the King's long-standing interests and the evolving role of the monarchy.

stories.title: 'Trading away honour': Congress slams PM Modi after reports of India seeking US waiver on Russian oil
stories.summary: India has reportedly sought an extension from the US to continue importing Russian oil, with the current waiver expiring May 16. The Congress party has sharply criticized PM Modi, accusing his government of "trading away India’s honour and dignity" and compromising energy security by "groveling before America" for permission.

stories.title: Unnao rape case: Supreme Court quashes Delhi HC order suspending Kuldeep Singh Sengar's life term
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has overturned the Delhi High Court's suspension of former BJP MLA Kuldeep Singh Sengar's life sentence in the Unnao rape case. The apex court has ordered the High Court to re-examine the matter within two months, ensuring a fresh decision free from prior influences.

stories.title: After NEET UG paper leak, education minister Dharmendra Pradhan announces computer-based exams from next year
stories.summary: Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan announced NEET UG exams will be computer-based from next year, emphasizing zero tolerance for malpractices amid paper leak allegations. A re-examination is scheduled for June 21st, with the investigation handed over to the CBI to address the examination mafia and ensure fairness for deserving students.

stories.title: NEET UG exam 2026 rescheduled for June 21 after paper leak row
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has announced a re-examination for NEET (UG) 2026 on Sunday, June 21, following the cancellation of the May 3 exam due to alleged irregularities. Investigators uncovered evidence of a "guess paper" with numerous questions closely matching the actual exam, prompting a CBI probe into the matter.

stories.title: 'Peace can't be piecemeal': India voices concern over Strait of Hormuz, Gaza at BRICS conclave
stories.summary: India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar urged BRICS nations to find practical solutions to geopolitical crises, emphasizing the threat to global energy and economic security from West Asian tensions. He stressed dialogue, diplomacy, and respect for sovereignty, while also highlighting concerns over unilateral sanctions, terrorism, and the need for UN Security Council reform.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi's fresh swipe at PM Modi over India-US trade deal: 'Compromised PM'
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi has accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of striking a "deal for Adani's release" with the US, rather than a genuine trade agreement. The Congress party echoed these sentiments, labeling the pact "one-sided" and alleging it aims to close fraud cases against Gautam Adani in America, suggesting Modi is compromised and subservient to US demands.

stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi begins a significant five-nation tour. He will visit the United Arab Emirates, Netherlands, Sweden, Norway, and Italy. The visits aim to boost India's engagement with Europe and the Gulf region. Discussions will focus on trade, investment, energy, and technology. This tour underscores India's growing global partnerships.

stories.title: ‘Xi would also like to see the Hormuz Strait open’: Trump on US-China talks
stories.summary: US President Trump revealed Chinese President Xi Jinping desires the Strait of Hormuz reopened to stabilize global energy markets. Both leaders reportedly agreed on the necessity of this crucial shipping route's resumption. Discussions also touched upon potential increased Chinese purchases of American oil and agricultural products, alongside ongoing tensions regarding Taiwan.

stories.title: 'Elections over, vasooli shuru': Opposition hits out at PM Modi over fuel hike with 'mahangayi man' jab
stories.summary: Fuel prices have increased across India. Petrol and diesel rates have gone up by Rs 3 per litre. Opposition parties are criticising the Modi government. They state that elections are over and price recovery has begun. This hike comes amid global energy price surges. India had previously absorbed these pressures. State-owned oil companies are now adjusting prices.

No evidence has publicly confirmed the claim, but the accusation has intensified Owens’ ongoing feud with Erika Kirk.

stories.title: Regulator bars 366 foreign-flagged ships from hiring Indian seafarers
stories.summary: India's maritime regulator has banned 366 foreign ships from hiring Indian sailors due to alleged abandonment, including unpaid wages and lack of compensation. These vessels, categorized as restricted or blacklisted, face immediate prohibition from employing Indian seafarers. The DG Shipping is demanding details of currently engaged Indian crew within two weeks.

The French first lady has denied the claims, while Farahani also rejected relationship rumors. The controversy comes as Owens continues fighting a defamation lawsuit filed by the French first couple over her past comments and online series.

stories.title: 5 massive pyramids still standing today: Why the largest one is not in Egypt
stories.summary: Ancient pyramids are often associated with Egypt. However, the largest pyramid ever built is in Mexico. The Great Pyramid of Cholula, known as Tlachihualtepetl, is a man-made mountain. It has a massive footprint, dwarfing the Great Pyramid of Giza in volume. This Mexican marvel is often overlooked, mistaken for a natural hill.

Both are in stable condition as authorities investigate the incident and Eatherly's controversial past.

The Progressive Party withdrew support after Silina dismissed the defense minister for failing to address drones flying from Russia. President Edgars Rinkevics will now consult parties to form a new government ahead of October elections.

stories.summary: Internet personality Clavicular went viral after admitting he used a hammer on his jaw as a teenager to improve his appearance. He said his parents even hid hammers to stop him. stories.title: 10 days of ‘manthan’ for Kerala’s ‘simhasanam’: Why Congress picked VD Satheesan over KC Venugopal

This move mirrors the Shiv Sena crisis and raises questions about AIADMK's future, its leadership, and control over its symbol.

stories.title: 'Janta mandate gone for a toss': BJP claims new Kerala CM will be 'remote controlled' by IUML

The Congress-led UDF's sweeping victory in the assembly elections triggered a fierce leadership race, with supporters of Satheesan, KC Venugopal, and Ramesh Chennithala campaigning vigorously. The party high command ultimately made the decision after extensive consultations.

stories.title: Crowdfunded Bid For Spirit: TikTok plan seeks to nationalise airline; over $330m pledged
stories.summary: Spirit Airlines has ceased operations after decades of making air travel affordable. TikTok founder Hunter Peterson has launched a movement to "nationalise" the airline with collective ownership. This initiative, inspired by the Green Bay Packers model, aims to shift focus from profit to service. Millions have pledged support, showing a growing trend in crowd-equity perception.

U.S. businessman Joel Weinshanker's Ad Populum, which manages Graceland, has acquired an 80% stake, aiming to boost visitor numbers from the US and Western Europe. This move blends pop culture with historical preservation, ensuring the castle's financial viability and continued allure.

This follows her appearance in lawyer's robes at the Calcutta High Court to argue a public interest litigation. The BCI seeks to verify her active status as an advocate, given her previous tenure as Chief Minister.

stories.title: UAE among world’s fastest-growing billionaire hubs with 17 residents worth $212.6 billion: Forbes
stories.summary: Indian-origin billionaires are increasingly powering the UAE's wealth, with nine individuals on Forbes Middle East's 2026 list commanding $49.9 billion. These entrepreneurs have built multi-billion-dollar businesses across various sectors, reflecting the UAE's appeal as a hub for global wealth due to its business-friendly policies and strategic location.

stories.title: The Xi exception: Why we saw a toned-down Trump in China
stories.summary: During a Beijing visit, President Trump observed China's military might, signaling a shift in global power. While the US faces munitions shortages and slow production, China's defense industry operates at wartime pace, excelling in drones, AI, and satellite tech. This evolving warfare, particularly concerning Taiwan, highlights a contest for future global dominance.

In 1913, Harry Brearley accidentally created stainless steel while testing rifle barrels
stories.summary: Sheffield metallurgist Harry Brearley's accidental 1913 discovery of corrosion-resistant steel, while seeking solutions for rifle barrel wear, revolutionized manufacturing. This practical, factory-floor innovation, born from routine testing, proved crucial for industries needing durable, hygienic materials. Stainless steel's enduring relevance highlights how addressing practical problems can lead to globally impactful, long-lasting inventions.

stories.title: In 1941, George de Mestral got annoyed by sticky burrs on his dog, and this accidentally launched the multibillion-dollar Velcro industry
stories.summary: Swiss engineer Georges de Mestral observed burrs attaching to his dog's fur, leading to the invention of Velcro. He discovered the burrs' hook-and-loop mechanism, which inspired a durable, reattachable fastener. NASA's adoption of Velcro for space missions further popularized this biomimicry innovation, showcasing nature's engineering solutions.

He also voiced concern over the West Asia crisis, emphasizing the need for uninterrupted maritime traffic and a sustained ceasefire in Gaza, advocating for a two-state solution.

stories.title: What is the ‘Thucydides Trap’? Why Xi Jinping brought it up during talks with Donald Trump in Beijing
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping invoked the "Thucydides Trap" during talks with US President Donald Trump, highlighting concerns that the rising power's growth could lead to conflict with the established dominant power. This theory, popularized by Graham Allison, suggests structural tensions make war more likely, a concept now central to global geopolitical debates involving trade wars and technological competition.

stories.title: UAE clarifies rules for workers changing jobs after contract ends, warns of one-year permit ban
stories.summary: UAE employees can now legally switch jobs after their contracts end or by mutual agreement, with the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation clarifying new rules. While job mobility has been eased, certain violations like unauthorized absence can still result in a one-year work permit ban.

stories.title: Why James Dyson kept building prototypes long after most people would quit? This reveals his billionaire invention rule
stories.summary: James Dyson's journey to invent the bagless vacuum cleaner involved 5,127 prototypes, highlighting the power of iterative design and learning from failure. This extensive process demonstrates that innovation stems from persistent testing, correction, and refinement rather than sudden inspiration. The story emphasizes that embracing failure as valuable data is crucial for product development and success.

stories.title: From evidence to action: The gaps in India’s maternal care
Carlos Slim's billionaire crisis rule about 'maintaining austerity in good times' is unexpectedly conservative
stories.summary: Billionaire Carlos Slim advocates for fiscal prudence during economic booms, a principle that strengthens companies for inevitable downturns. This approach counters the tendency for excessive spending and hidden inefficiencies that high revenues often mask. By focusing on waste prevention and retaining flexibility, businesses build resilience, enabling them to navigate crises without drastic measures.

stories.title: The 5 deepest ocean trenches on Earth: Why one basin owns every single slot
stories.summary: All of Earth's deepest ocean trenches are located in the Pacific Ocean, a result of intense tectonic plate subduction. These trenches, like the Mariana and Tonga, are formed where oceanic plates dive beneath continental plates, creating geological wounds. These dynamic features offer clues to Earth's self-transformation and the potential for life elsewhere.

stories.title: America’s first social philanthropist: The secret story of 5,000 schools and a generosity second to none
stories.summary: During segregation, African Americans faced inadequate education. Businessman Julius Rosenwald partnered with Booker T. Washington and local communities to build over 5,000 schools. This initiative, funded by matching grants and community contributions, provided vital educational spaces. These schools became community hubs, fostering literacy and self-respect. Though many are gone, their legacy highlights community power in overcoming systemic neglect.

stories.title: The hidden ocean: Why Australia’s invisible underground water system is larger than the entire state of Alaska
stories.summary: Beneath Australia's arid outback lies a vast, hidden underground ocean, the Great Artesian Basin, larger than Alaska. This ancient water source, some two million years old, is under immense pressure, naturally flowing to the surface through bores. This subterranean marvel sustains billions in economic activity, supports towns, agriculture, and unique desert oasis, proving that the most vital elements are often unseen.

stories.title: 89 killed as thunderstorm batters Uttar Pradesh

stories.summary: French authorities have eased restrictions on the cruise ship Ambition after confirming a viral gastrointestinal outbreak, not hantavirus, sickened dozens. Around 80 passengers and crew experienced symptoms, with no severe cases reported. A passenger's death was attributed to a heart attack, unrelated to the illness. The ship, carrying over 1,700 people, was temporarily restricted as a precaution.

stories.title: Hantavirus outbreak: Deadly Andes strain detected in cruise ship cases; 8 cases confirmed
stories.summary: A hantavirus outbreak linked to the cruise ship MV Hondius has seen eight passengers test positive for the Andes virus, a strain known to spread between humans. Three lives have been lost so far. While the risk to the general public is low, passengers and crew are under quarantine for 42 days as investigations continue.

stories.title: 'US, China should be partners not rivals': Key takeaways from Trump and Xi's much-watched summit
